title: Last Stone Weight
summary: Given an array of integers representing the weights of stones, repeatedly select the two heaviest stones, smash them together, and continue until at most one stone remains.
statement: Given an array of integers representing the weights of stones, repeatedly select the two heaviest stones, smash them together, and continue until at most one stone remains. If the two stones have the same weight, both are destroyed. If they have different weights, the lighter stone is destroyed, and the heavier stone's weight is reduced by the weight of the lighter stone. Return the weight of the last remaining stone, or 0 if all stones are destroyed.
constraints: Repeatedly smash the two greatest weights.
Return the last weight or zero when none remains.
hints: Python’s min-heap can represent a max-heap by negating weights.
Pop two largest; push their positive difference only when unequal.
Continue until at most one heap entry remains.
Each loop exactly simulates one mandated smash and preserves all remaining weights.
editorial: Each loop exactly simulates one mandated smash and preserves all remaining weights.

tests.explanation: A sole stone is already the result.
